agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading
COVID-19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s
Order (revised September 22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will
be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which
will be live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged
to submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item
you would like to speak on has been called and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to
speak and to download the Zoom application.

Programs activities.

WORK PLAN: This item includes projects included in the Adopted Work Plan for Fiscal
Year 2022-2023.

DISCUSSION: Environmental Programs staff will provide a presentation that will detail
the City’s current environmental program activities, including energy, water conservation,
pollution prevention, waste reduction, coastal, and events and outreach. Although some
projects have been added to the Adopted Work Plan, other assignments are ongoing and
part of normal staff operations. The Adopted Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2022-2023
included the following tasks: Dark Sky implementation, Clean Power Alliance, clean water,
coastal vulnerability assessment, dumpster locking lid enforcement, and compliance with
State and Regional requirements.

Subject:  Dark Sky Program Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION:  Receive an update on enforcement of the City’s Dark Sky
Ordinance.

WORK PLAN:  This item was included as Item 5.l. in the Adopted Work Plan for Fiscal
Year 2022-2023.

DISCUSSION: The City’s Dark Sky Ordinance (Dark Sky) is contained in Malibu Municipal
Code Chapter 17.41 and became effective on October 15, 2018. Dark Sky is meant to
protect Malibu's environment and community quality of life from light pollution. On January
13, 2022, the City Council amended the Dark Sky compliance deadlines for all zoning
districts, except for parcels with service stations. The deadlines are as follows:

  • October 15, 2019 - Outdoor lighting at gas station properties
  • October 15, 2022 - Outdoor lighting in commercial and residential zones

Gas Stations

In 2019, City staff began working with the owners of gas station properties. Only one of
six service stations has demonstrated full compliance (Chevron located at 23670 Pacific
Coast Highway). The remaining five service stations have submitted Planning
applications. All five have shown they can comply with every aspect of Dark Sky except
for the light trespass requirement along property lines that are adjacent to the public right-
of-way. On August 22, 2022, City Council again amended Dark Sky to allow a light

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item 3.C.
 trespass limit for commercially and institutionally zoned properties onto the public right-of-
way. This will not conflict with the intent of Dark Sky as the public rights-of-way are already
lit with streetlights that have a higher luminosity than the anticipated light trespass from
the adjacent properties.

Outreach Efforts

In 2022, staff developed an outreach and educational plan to inform businesses and the
public about these regulations. The goal was to draw attention to the October 15 deadline.

  • Virtual Meetings: The City hosted four virtual presentations for Commercial and
  Residential property owners.

  • Website: Planning applications, checklists, requirements by zoning district, and
  contact information is available at www.malibucity.org/DarkSky.

  • Electronic Notifications: Multiple social media posts (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram,
  and NextDoor) and e-notifications via email/text were sent.

  • Print Advertising: Two banners were posted in high-visibility locations and Program
  information was advertised in The Malibu Times.

  • Handouts: Manta Publications designed posters, and staff distributed them to post
  offices, grocery stores, schools, and City facilities. Postcards were also mailed to all
  businesses and residents.

Program Summary

The Dark Sky Program is intended to protect the community through effective lighting
policies and environmentally responsible outdoor lighting. Staff also conducted four virtual
community workshops for commercial and residential sectors. To date, the City has issued
21 electrical (Dark Sky) permits, eight of which are completed.

In January 2023, staff submitted Dark Sky for award consideration to: 1) Southern
California Association of Governments (SCAG) for the Plan, Policy, and Program
category; and 2) American Planning Association for the Community-Wide Program
category. These awards are for projects that go above and beyond the requirements for
natural resource conservation and city beautification.

Staff will continue outreach efforts since the goal of the Dark Sky Program is to preserve
Malibu’s rural appeal and to protect local wildlife from light pollution. Additionally, staff’s
approach to enforcement focuses on education and will include site visits and a tiered
structure for notice of violations.
